title: Area of Regular Polygons and Composite Figures
seo_title: Geometry Area of Regular Polygons and Composite Figures Worksheets (TEKS G.11A)
short_title: Area of Regular Polygons and Composite Figures
standard_text: G.11A apply the formula for the area of regular polygons to solve problems using appropriate units of measure; G.11B determine the area of composite two-dimensional figures comprised of a combination of triangles, parallelograms, trapezoids, kites, regular polygons, or sectors of circles to solve problems using appropriate units of measure
meta_desc: Free Geometry worksheets for Texas TEKS G.11A and G.11B: area of regular polygons with the apothem, trapezoids, kites and composite figures. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Composite: add the parts, subtract the holes.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Area of a regular polygon: A = ½aP, where a is the apothem and P the perimeter.
  • The apothem goes from the center to the middle of a side, at a right angle.
  • Trapezoid: ½(b1 + b2)h. Kite or rhombus: ½d1d2.
  • Composite figures: split into simple shapes and add; subtract any holes.

Examples

Example

Regular hexagon, side 10, apothem 8.7

P = 60

½ × 8.7 × 60

Answer: 261 square units

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using the side instead of the perimeterP = n × side.
Forgetting ½A = ½aP.
Adding a holeSubtract the cut-out part.

items.q: A picture frame is 40 cm by 25 cm on the outside. The wood is 5 cm wide all round. What is the area of the wood?
items.e: Outside 40 × 25 = 1,000 square centimeters. Inside (40 − 10) × (25 − 10) = 30 × 15 = 450 square centimeters. Wood = 550 square centimeters.

items.e: Backyard 21 × 12 = 252 square meters. Garden bed 3 × 6 = 18 square meters. Lawn = 234 square meters.
